hints.title: Distances to Reachable Nodes
hints.text: Each node has at most one outgoing edge, so traversal from node1 and node2 follows simple path chains.

hints.title: Distance Arrays
hints.text: Compute the shortest distance from node1 to every reachable node, and separately from node2 to every reachable node.

hints.title: Minimizing Peak Distance
hints.text: Iterate through all nodes i. Find a node reachable from both that minimizes max(dist1[i], dist2[i]), breaking ties by smallest index.

hints.title: Chain Traversal and Distance Minimization Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def closestMeetingNode(self, edges: list[int], node1: int, node2: int) -> int:
        def get_dists(start):
            dist = [-1] * len(edges)
            cur = start
            d = 0
            while cur != -1 and dist[cur] == -1:
                dist[cur] = d
                d += 1
                cur = edges[cur]
            return dist
        d1 = get_dists(node1)
        d2 = get_dists(node2)
        min_dist = float('inf')
        ans = -1
        for i in range(len(edges)):
            if d1[i] != -1 and d2[i] != -1:
                mx = max(d1[i], d2[i])
                if mx < min_dist:
                    min_dist = mx
                    ans = i
        return ans
```

variables: n: number of nodes in graph
complexity.notes: Linear path traversal since each node has out-degree at most 1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-running graph searches for every candidate destination takes O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Distance arrays store step counts for all n nodes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Precomputes distances from both starting nodes and finds meeting point minimizing max distance.
